Displacement Reaction: why does an iron nail in blue copper sulphate get a reddish-brown layer? It's copper. Class 10 Chemistry, Chemical Reactions and Equations.

• Iron is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper from copper sulphate solution
• Copper is deposited on the nail as a reddish-brown coating
• The blue solution fades to light green as iron sulphate forms
• Fe(s) + CuSO4(aq) → FeSO4(aq) + Cu(s), and it is balanced
